learningObjectives: Understand JWT-based authentication and token flow.
Identify common security practices for full stack applications.

activities.title: Authentication vs Authorization
activities.instruction: Choose the security concept that matches each scenario.

content.concept: Authentication verifies who a user is, while authorization determines what an authenticated user is allowed to access or perform.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Checking a password to verify a user's identity → Authentication
Checking whether a user can access an admin page → Authorization
config.answer: Checking a password to verify a user's identity → Authentication

activities.title: JWT Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the three main parts of a JSON Web Token.

content.concept: A JWT is commonly represented as three dot-separated parts: a header describing the token type and algorithm, a payload containing claims, and a signature used to verify integrity.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Contains metadata such as the token type and signing algorithm.
Contains claims such as user or role information.
Provides a cryptographic integrity check for the signed token.

activities.title: Authentication Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the basic login and protected-request flow.

content.concept: A token-based authentication flow verifies credentials, issues a token, and uses that token when accessing protected resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 4. Client stores the token according to the application's security design
5. Client sends the token with a protected request
6. Server verifies the token and authorization

activities.title: Security Strategy Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the security practice that best addresses each scenario.

content.concept: Full stack applications should use practices such as password hashing, input validation, secure transport, access control, safe token handling, and protection against common web attacks.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Store user passwords using a secure password-hashing algorithm
Store user passwords as plain text
config.answer: Store user passwords using a secure password-hashing algorithm
